content: Chloroquine and certain drugs can both prolong the QTc interval, which increases the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. The following interactions and recommendations are noted: 1. Chloroquine and Buprenorphine (subdermal implant, transdermal, or long-acting injection): Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug due to the serious risk of arrhythmias. 2. Chloroquine and Bupropion: Bupropion increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Chloroquine and Calcium Carbonate: Calcium carbonate reduces chloroquine absorption through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate doses by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 4. Chloroquine and Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Chloroquine and Carvedilol: Chloroquine increases carvedilol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor closely for potential toxicity. 6. Chloroquine and Ceritinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and ceritinib increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Chloroquine and Chlorpromazine: Chloroquine increases chlorpromazine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval and inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Chloroquine and Cholera Vaccine: Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administer the vaccine at least 10 days before starting chloroquine. 9. Chloroquine and Cimetidine: Cimetidine increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Chloroquine and Ciprofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, especially in patients with other risk factors for QT prolongation. 11. Chloroquine and Cisapride: Chloroquine increases cisapride toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Chloroquine and Citalopram: Chloroquine increases citalopram toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Chloroquine and Clarithromycin: Chloroquine increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, and clarithromycin increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Chloroquine and Clobazam: Clobazam increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose adjustments may be required. 15. Chloroquine and Clofazimine: Chloroquine increases clofazimine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Chloroquine and Clomipramine: Chloroquine increases clomipramine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval and inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Chloroquine and Clozapine: Chloroquine increases clozapine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Chloroquine and Codeine: Chloroquine inhibits the conversion of codeine to its active metabolite morphine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Chloroquine and Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Chloroquine and Crizotinib: Chloroquine increases crizotinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, and crizotinib increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Chloroquine and Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut. Use caution and monitor closely. 22.
